quandoUsar: Showing a hierarchy of parts of a whole, such as revenue by business line and product, when relative size matters more than exact comparisons.
Exploring by levels: clicking a block zooms that branch to fill the view, and the breadcrumb at the top goes back to any level above.
Showing a second measure, such as growth, in color intensity, with `colorLabel` and a stepped scale below the chart.
quandoEvitar: Use `bar-chart` when the reader needs to compare values precisely: areas are hard to compare by eye.
Use `composition-chart` or `donut-chart` for a few parts at a single level.
Use `tree-table` when each node of the hierarchy needs exact numbers in columns.

teclado.acao: With focus on the chart, jump to the nearest first-level block in that direction.
Go to the first or last first-level block, in the order of `data`.
Zoom into the focused block, when it has children, and move the highlight to the first child.
Go up one level and highlight the block it came from; at the root, remove the highlight.

acessibilidade: The block area is a focusable group with `aria-roledescription="treemap"` and the instructions in its name, in English; the keyboard moves through the first-level blocks of the view only.
An `aria-live="polite"` region reads the active block (path, value, share of its parent, and the color measure), and a hidden table lists all nodes with path and values.
The breadcrumb is a `<nav>` with an ordered list and `aria-current="location"` on the current level; the tooltip is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
movimento: The first time on screen, blocks grow from their own center, in a quick wave that starts with the largest.
When zooming in, the chosen block grows to fill the view and the children appear; when going back, the view shrinks to it; with new data, each block resizes in place.
With “reduced motion” on, each change goes straight to the final layout, the tooltip doesn't glide, and the breadcrumb swaps without displacement.
responsivo: The width follows the container and the height is fixed by `height` (420 px); name and value only appear on blocks with room (over 64 × 38 px), and small ones depend on the tooltip.
On touch there is no hover tooltip: tapping a block zooms into its branch, and tapping a first-level leaf shows its numbers.
desempenho: Every node in the tree has a DOM element, even out of view, `data` is serialized on every render, and the animation repositions blocks in JavaScript on every frame; with thousands of leaves, aggregate first.
notasIA: Pass a root in `data` (`{ id, label, children }`) with `value` only on leaves: a branch's value is the sum of its children, and the root's `label` starts the breadcrumb.
To color by the second measure, give `color` to the leaves and pass `colorLabel` (and `formatColor`); the first four branches get a series hue and the rest stay neutral.
`focus` with `onFocusChange` controls the zoomed branch (a leaf id shows the root); keep the `id`s stable between datasets so blocks transform instead of reappearing.
